reviewConcept: Interpret SQL as set-oriented processing with grouping over rows.

explanation: Option A correctly joins products to their August 2026 sales, restricts rows to that month with a bounded date range, and groups by product so each product appears once with its total quantity sold. B lists individual sale rows instead of totals, C finds products with sales but does not return the total quantity, and D is not the best answer because it selects `p.name` without grouping by it.

options.text:
SELECT p.product_id, p.name, SUM(s.qty) AS total_qty
FROM Product p
JOIN Sale s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE s.sale_date >= DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND s.sale_date < DATE '2026-09-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.name;

SELECT p.product_id, p.name, s.qty
FROM Product p
JOIN Sale s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE s.sale_date >= DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND s.sale_date < DATE '2026-09-01';

SELECT p.product_id, p.name
FROM Product p
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM Sale s
  WHERE s.product_id = p.product_id
    AND s.sale_date >= DATE '2026-08-01'
    AND s.sale_date < DATE '2026-09-01'
);

SELECT p.product_id, p.name, SUM(s.qty) AS total_qty
FROM Product p
LEFT JOIN Sale s ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE s.sale_date >= DATE '2026-08-01'
  AND s.sale_date < DATE '2026-09-01'
GROUP BY p.product_id;
